sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 13:134

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 13:134:1
items.html:
Certainly there are illuminations that also issue from Mocha Stimaa to the outside, etc., that the lights mingle together and become clothed within the Nimin [strands] of hair, although the Nimin are more superior than they are: As said above, that there are three Havayot in the Chivaret [bright strands], because three heads are included together in them: the two Havayot of right and left, which are opposite the face, are the discernment of Mem, Lamed, which are drawn from Galgalta and the Mocha of the air. And the Havaya that is behind the Rosh [head] is the discernment of Tzadi, which is drawn from Mocha Stimaa [the concealed brain], as above. Thus, the discernment of Mocha Stimaa is also included in the Nimin and the Chivaret.
And this is what he said: “since the lights rise from within Mocha Stimaa, etc., of necessity the lights mingle together and become clothed within the Nimin of hair, etc., and they are like the Jordan, whose waters pass through the Sea of Tiberias without mingling” — meaning, as above, that the lights of Mocha Stimaa are also included in all the Nimin, except that above, upon the Galgalta, they do not mingle; rather, those that belong to the discernment of Mocha Stimaa come in the Havaya behind the Rosh, and those that belong to the two heads, Galgalta and the air, come in the two Havayot of right and left of the face.
